lesson_title: Bend the Ruler: What an Earthquake Actually Is
hook_text: A 7 isn't 'a bit worse' than a 5. It's a thousand times more energy.
clip_script: Hold a plastic ruler at both ends and bend it. It doesn't break straight away — it bends, and it stores your effort inside itself. You can feel it pushing back. Bend further. Further. SNAP. Both halves whip back straight and your hands feel the jolt. That is an earthquake, exactly. Plates push, the fault is stuck by friction, the rock just bends and stores the energy — sometimes for centuries. Then one day it can't hold, the fault slips, the rock springs back, and everything stored leaves at once. The point underground where it snapped is the focus. The spot on the surface right above it is the epicentre. Now the number people get wrong. The Richter scale isn't a normal ruler — every step up is ten times more shaking and about thirty-two times more energy. So a 7 next to a 5 is two steps: a hundred times the movement, and about a thousand times the energy. Never say 'slightly stronger'. And the hard truth underneath all of it: earthquakes don't kill people. Falling buildings do.
visual_style: Extreme close-up of a ruler flexing and snapping, cutting to a cross-section of ground with the focus glowing underground and the epicentre marked on the surface above.
mood: Tense build, sharp release, sober landing.
pacing: Slow tension on the bend, hard cut at the snap, brisk through the numbers, quiet final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how the epicentre is found and how buildings are made to survive.
